definitions.explanation: Having an excessive desire for money, possessions, or other things. Always negative.

examples.japanese: {欲深|よくふか}い{人|ひと}は{嫌|きら}われる。
あの{地主|じぬし}は{欲深|よくふか}くて{有名|ゆうめい}だ。
examples.english: That landlord is known for being greedy.

examples.japanese: {欲深|よくふか}い{王様|おうさま}が{民|たみ}から{税|ぜい}を{搾|しぼ}り{取|と}った。
examples.english: The greedy king squeezed taxes out of the people.

examples.japanese: {人間|にんげん}は{欲深|よくふか}い{生|い}き{物|もの}で、{満足|まんぞく}を{知|し}らない。
examples.english: Humans are greedy creatures who never know satisfaction.

notes:
A compound i-adjective formed from {欲|よく} (desire, greed) + {深|ふか}い (deep). Describes someone whose desires run deep — excessively wanting money, power, or material things. Always used negatively.

ETYMOLOGY:
Literally "deep in desire." The compound structure is transparent: {欲|よく} (desire) + {深|ふか}い (deep).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {欲深|よくふか}い{人|ひと}: a greedy person
- {欲深|よくふか}い{目|め}: greedy eyes
- {欲深|よくふか}い{商人|しょうにん}: a greedy merchant

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {貪欲|どんよく}な: greedy, covetous (more formal and literary)
- {強欲|ごうよく}な: avaricious, rapacious (stronger, more extreme)
- {欲張|よくば}り: greedy person, greediness (more colloquial noun/na-adjective)
- がめつい: greedy, stingy (very colloquial, Kansai origin)

forms.label: Conditional たら
forms.negative: {欲深|よくふか}くなかったら
